lookback_notes: NOT_FOUND — the protocol's Area 13 entry (p. 11) states only the audit criterion for an incorrect rate code and lists regulatory references; it does not state any observation/look-back window for this finding. (A 7-day look-back is stated elsewhere in the document for the PRI in Area 30, p. 18, but that is a different finding area and is not applied to Area 13 here.)

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the rate code billed is not the correct rate code for the services provided, the difference between the appropriate claim amount and the paid claim amount will be disallowed.

state_deltas.delta: Area 13 (Incorrect Rate Code Billed) is a New York OMIG audit finding area applicable to the Assisted Living Program for service dates 01/01/2013 through 10/31/2025; the disallowance is the difference between the appropriate claim amount and the paid claim amount.

Regulatory references cited for this finding include 18 NYCRR § 504.3(f), (h), and (i); 18 NYCRR § 505.35(h)(1); and the NYS Medicaid Program Assisted Living Program (ALP) Manual, Policy Guidelines Version 2006-1, Section I.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The finding directly governs payment: an incorrect rate code results in disallowance of the difference between the appropriate and paid claim amounts. The cited references include the UAS-NY memo on generating RUG III scores and calculating hours of formal care, tying rate code determination to the RUG-based classification. The document does not further explain the rate-code-to-case-mix mechanics.
